title: Test Your Understanding: Design a Web Crawler
description: Politeness, dedup, frontier queues, and distributed fetch — from the case study.

questions.question: Why use per-host queues in the URL frontier?

options.text: HTML parses faster on single-host batches
To enforce politeness — limit request rate per site without starving others
robots.txt only applies to global queues
DNS requires one queue per TLD

questions.explanation: A global FIFO lets workers hammer one domain. Per-host queues + rate limits spread load and reduce blocks.

questions.question: URL normalization before dedup primarily prevents:

options.text: HTTPS certificate errors
Fetching the same resource under different URL strings
robots.txt parsing failures
Worker OOM from large pages

questions.explanation: http vs https, trailing slashes, fragments, and tracking params can alias the same page. Normalize to one canonical key.

questions.question: A Bloom filter in dedup helps because:

options.text: It stores full HTML in compressed form
It cheaply rejects URLs definitely not seen before (with rare false positives)
It replaces robots.txt
It guarantees exactly-once fetch

questions.explanation: Bloom filters use little RAM to test membership. 'Definitely not seen' skips enqueue; 'maybe' confirms against durable store.

questions.question: On HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests), a crawler should:

options.text: Double concurrent workers for that host
Retry immediately in a tight loop
Backoff and reduce rate for that host
Ignore and continue at same rate

questions.explanation: 429 is the site asking you to slow down. Exponential backoff and lower per-host concurrency prevent IP bans.

questions.question: Decoupling fetch and parse with blob storage means:

options.text: Parser runs inside the HTTP client thread
Fetch stores raw page; parse workers read blobs asynchronously
HTML is never stored
Frontier is eliminated

questions.explanation: Network-bound fetchers stay fast; CPU-heavy parse scales separately. Failed parse can retry without re-fetching.

questions.question: robots.txt should be consulted:

options.text: After storing HTML, to delete disallowed pages
Before fetching a URL — skip if disallowed for your user-agent
Only for government domains
Once per crawl run globally

questions.explanation: Fetch and cache robots per host; check allow/disallow before issuing GET. Technical and legal politeness.

questions.question: At-least-once queue delivery means fetch workers should be idempotent when storing pages.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Redelivered jobs may re-fetch the same URL. Store by url_hash or upsert metadata so retries don't corrupt state.

questions.question: Which can cause infinite or runaway crawl? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Calendar pagination with unlimited ?page=N links
Per-host rate limiting
Session IDs in every URL without normalization
Bloom filter dedup

questions.explanation: Faceted navigation and unique-session URLs explode the frontier. Rate limits and dedup help; you also need depth limits and URL pattern policies.
